findings.title: Cached getForLogin results are not invalidated when an organization changes
findings.body: The login cache is keyed per realm and fetch mode and is invalidated only on IDP create, update and remove. getByOrganization also checks isInvalid(orgId), but getForLogin does not. Organization changes that affect login IDPs (an IDP linked to or unlinked from an org, or an org enabled/disabled or removed) are not covered by the update path in this class. The cached set can then go stale, and IDPs can be returned that should no longer be shown.

findings.title: Cache holds one entry per fetch mode and handles other organization IDs poorly
findings.body: The cache key does not include the organization id, so a single query per FetchMode holds all searchKeys. Every new organizationId triggers invalidateObject(cacheKey) and rebuilds the query. That evicts and rewrites the entry on each distinct org, and when many orgs alternate the cache thrashes and gives little benefit. The invalidateObject call also broadcasts a cluster invalidation on what is a read path.

findings.title: Cached results are not filtered for current login eligibility
findings.body: Cached IDs are resolved through getById, which returns the cached model without re-checking the login predicate. If an IDP changed in a way that does not trigger login invalidation, it is still returned. For example, a transition from REALM to an org with BROKER_PUBLIC changed would be missed by the skip logic. The enabled state is re-checked only in the caller bean, so other callers of getForLogin get unfiltered results.

findings.title: remove() performs an extra DB lookup on every call
findings.body: remove() now calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) unconditionally, even when the alias is cached and the lookup is not needed for the existing invalidation path. This adds a database query on every removal. storedIdp can also be null if the alias does not exist, and the code then relies on getLoginPredicate's nonNull check.
